description.narrative:
IDI's vision, and hence the contribution's overall objective, is: Effective public external audit by Supreme Audit Institutions (SAIs) promotes transparency and accountability, effective public financial management, good governance, improved service delivery, fights corruption and contributes to poverty reduction and sustainable development.
The vision is followed by a mission-statement, core-principles and four objectives with three intermediate objectives each. These objectives are all clearly linked to performance-indicators, outputs, outcomes and impact as well as to baselines and targets. The four objectives constitute "work streams", meaning that IDI works with these areas continuously and not only as program objectives to be achieved over a short period of time.
The four objectives in IDI's strategic plan are: Independent SAIs, Well governed SAIs, Professional SAIs and Relevant SAIs. IDI's four objectives constitute "work streams" which implies that they are objectives on a very high level and not likely to be achieved for all SAIs at the end of the period (2023). Rather IDI will work to take steps towards those goals for the target group of SAIs during the program period.

INTOSAI Development Initiative (IDI) hereby applies for a continued core support for its new Strategic Plan 2019-2023, for the period 1 January 2019- 31 December 2019. The applied total amount is 75 000 000 SEK, amounting to 12-14 % of IDI’s total budget for the entire Strategic Plan.
The International Organisation for Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI) is a non-profit umbrella organization of Supreme Audit Institutions (SAI) across the world with 194-member countries. INTOSAI Development Initiative (IDI) is a non-profit, autonomous INTOSAI body, mandated to support SAI's in developing countries to sustainably enhance their performance and capacity. The IDI also serves as secretariat to the INTOSAI-Donor Cooperation. IDI was established in 1986 as an INTOSAI training body, and is currently located in Oslo, Norway. IDI receives a significant portion of its core funding based on an Act of the Norwegian Parliament, passed when IDI was transferred to Norway in 2001, where it is established under Norwegian Foundation Law. Except Norway, other core support donors are (Sweden), Austria, Estonia, DFID, European Commission and INTOSAI. A number of donors with earmarked-support are i.e. France, Canada, Saudi Arabia, Iceland.
IDI has presented a more ambitious Strategic Plan for 2019-2023. The increased ambition lies in a new working method, so-called work streams with a new results matrix, increased focus on quality in the capacity development and increased focus on support and a full integration of gender mainstreaming throughout the Strategic Plan; from gender analysis of specific projects to gender mainstreamed activities and gender-mainstreamed selection of participants, trainers and workplans.
IDIs Strategic Plan aims at capacity strengthening of the Supreme Audit Institutions (SAI’s) in developing countries and in fragile countries through need-based and locally anchored programmes involving trainings, technical support and organisational development. Sida assesses IDI to have the mandate, expertise, systems, networks and long-term experience of conducting capacity development programmes of SAI’s in developing countries, and can therefor contribute to rule of law through its contribution to increased transparency, accountability, and improved service delivery, benefiting all citizens, and mostly the most poor.

Insatsen avser ett kärnstöd till den internationella organisationen för riksrevisioner, the International Organisation for Supreme Audit Institutions, INTOSAI Development Initiative (IDI), om totalt 75 000 000 SEK under en fem års-period med startdatum 1 januari 2019 till och med 31 december 2023. Insatsen syftar till att kapacitetstärka riksrevisioner i utvecklingsländer genom ett behovs- och efterfrågansbaserat arbete bestående av utbildningar, informationsspridning och tekniskt stöd.
INTOSAI är en icke-vinstdrivande paraplyorganisation för riksrevisioner över hela världen. INTOSAI har 194 medlemsländer och ar en regional organisationsstruktur med underorganisationer och diverse kommittér och arbetsgrupper. INTOSAI har ett kapacitetsutvecklingsorgan; INTOSAI Development Initiative (IDI) som är registrerad som en separat enhet och är icke-vinstdrivande organisation. IDI har haft kärnstöd från Sida de senaste 15 åren och de har härmed inkommit med en ny ansökan om förnyat kärnstöd om 75 000 000 SEK som täcker perioden för IDI's nya strategiska plan, 2019-2023. Den totala budgeten för IDI 2019-2023 är ca 579 228 196 SEK, det föreslagna Sida stödet om 75 000 000 uppgår till ca 12-14 % av den totala budgeten. Det innebär en procentuell minskning från föregående kärnstödperiod - 2014-2018, då den totala IDI budgeten uppgick till ca 220 000 000 SEK - då Sida stödet uppgick till ca 18%. Den procentuella minskningen, trots den stora totala budgetökningen, härleds till utökat stöd från traditionella givare samt nyförvärv av nya givare. Kärnstödsgivarna är i följande storleksordning; Norge, Sverige/Sida, Österrike, Estland, DFID, Europeiska Kommissionen samt INTOSAI. Bland givare med öronmärkt stöd finns t ex; Frankrike, Canada, Saudi Arabien, Island m.fl.
IDI bedöms av Sida ha mandat, kompetens i form av expertis, system, nätverk och erfarenhet att bedriva ett kapacitetsutvecklande program av riksrevisioner i utvecklingsländer i syfte att bidra till de svenska prioriteringarna och till att rättsstatens principer i högre grad kan råda i de kontexter programmen verkar i.
IDI har en ny och mer ambitiös strategisk plan för 2019-2023. Den ökade ambitionen består av en ny arbetsmodell med mer fokus på kvalité och stöd, anpassade efter lokala behov och rekommendationer från en halvtidsöversyn genomförd av Sida. Den ökande ambitionen består även av en genderintegration av hela den strategiska planen, från genderanalys av samtliga insatser och aktiviteter till genomförande och urval av aktiviteter, deltagare, föreläsare och arbetsplaner.

The results are presented according to which workstream they belong to; Independent SAIs, Well-Governed SAIs, Professional SAIs, Relevant SAIs, Bilateral Support, Global Foundations
Under Independant SAIs Sida notices the conclusion that SAI is part of a broader accountability ecosystem. IDI partners and collaborates with the INTOSAI-Donor Cooperation, Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative, World Justice Project, OECD, IMF, Transparency International, World Bank & CSOs around the world.
Examples of results from the period 2019-2024:
Well-governed SAIs: 55 SAIs submitted audit reports to relevant authorities on the institutional framework for fighting corruption
Professional SAIs: The SAI-auditor training PESA was established as regular certification for SAI auditors, on which all SAIs can rely, over 100 SAIs have staff enrolled in PESA
Relevant SAIs, 13 SAIs in Latin American and the Caribbean (OLACEF) published audit reports on sustainable public procurement contributing to green and inclusive growth. Audit and education support for 48 SAIs in English and Spanish, launched with INTOSAI Working Group on Environmental Audit, covering four themes; Implementation of climate change adaptation plans & actions, Disaster risk reduction, Water resources management, Sea level rise and coastal erosion.
The bilateral support has contributed to results in challenging contexts such as Democratic Republic of Congo, Madagascar, Somalia, South Sudan, The Gambia, Niger.
An example from the workstream on Global Foundations is the cooperation with IPU (Inter-Parliamentary Union) that brought together 350 SAI leaders and parliamentarians from 97 countries.
The report also shows how SAI Independence continues to regress, and how more SAIs face restrictions in selecting their audit programmes, OLACEFS and CAROSAI (Caribbean) being especially challenged.
The report summarizes the most serious risks and threats to long-lasting results.
External shocks to the SAI institutional environment are the key threat to sustainable improvement, these are:
Shutting down the SAI Unlawfully removing/suspending the SAI Head Withdrawing/withholding the funds needed for the SAI to operate Undermining SAI credibility amongst the public
Based on this IDI identifies learnings for the furture support to SAIs, among those learnings are to build alliances with other actors in the accountability ecosystem.
In the words of IDI:
Through Sidas support to IDI over the years, a number of important initiatives took off or continued, such as: - The SAI Performance Measurement Framework (SAI PMF), a framework for holistic and evidence-based evaluation of SAI performance. - Holistic support to nine challenged SAIs in Africa, the Accelerated Peer-Support Partnership (PAP-APP). It is a success and has been followed by support to eight more challenged SAIs globally through the Global SAI Accountability Initiative (GSAI). - The SAI Independence Rapid Advocacy Mechanism (SIRAM) which provides timely and coordinated responses to independence threats to SAIs all over the world - Professional Education for SAI Auditors (PESA) providing SAI audit staff globally the opportunity to access a comprehensive, online, inclusive, professional audit education certificate, already delivered in English and Spanish with plans to offer this in annually also in Arabic and French. - Auditing the SDGs as a SAI contribution to strengthening, following up and reviewing the implementation of SDGs. - Advocating for putting gender equality on the agenda of INTOSAI and SAIs and supporting gender audits (see the video on our website: https://www.idi.no/cross-cutting-priorities/inclusiveness-and-gender)
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
